clue.text: Legs cut doing a backflip

indicators.note: a backflip turns something over end to end, so the word for cut is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: to snip is to cut with scissors

explanation.surface: A gymnast's legs get injured while turning a backflip.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins is informal slang for a person's legs, as in 'shaky on his pins'.

clue.text: God thus climbing above goddess

indicators.note: in a down entry, being above means coming first, so this piece is placed before the goddess
in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the word for thus is read bottom to top

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: A god clambering up and positioning himself over a goddess, like a scene from mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian deity of the afterlife and the dead.

clue.text: Measure bringing age into focus

indicators.note: bringing one thing into another puts it inside, as the clue's 'into' confirms

parts.note: the centre is the focus or central point
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A step that brings the passage of age into sharp focus, like a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' completes the insertion phrase: the age word sits inside the focus word.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a unit of length, a hundredth of a metre.

clue.text: Into the embrace of father, that girl ran

indicators.note: something taken into an embrace is held inside the arms, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
the pronoun for that girl

explanation.surface: A little girl runs into her father's open arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to run quickly, so dashed is a past-tense synonym of ran.

clue.text: English king and James VI, say, both briefly outside

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, and both applies it to each of the two names, so each loses its last letter

parts.note: Alfred the Great, the Anglo-Saxon king
James VI was King of Scots, so he is an example of a Scot

explanation.surface: Two historical kings, one English and one Scottish, briefly stepping outside together.
explanation.walkthrough: James VI of Scotland later also became James I of England; here he is simply an example of a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco, from Italian, means in the open air, so an alfresco meal is eaten outside.

clue.text: Back on summit in Greece, very excited

indicators.note: in a down entry, placed on means sitting above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: back as in 'years back', meaning ago

indicators.note: in a down entry the summit of a word is its top, meaning its first letter

parts.note: the top letter of Greece

explanation.surface: A climber back on top of a mountain in Greece is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Greek mountain top; 'Back' is really a time word, and 'summit in Greece' only means its top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes someone eager and keenly expectant, full of excitement.

clue.text: Financial promise broken by broadcaster, that's for sure!

indicators.note: a thing broken by another is split open with the other wedged in the gap

parts.note: an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt
telly is British slang for television, a broadcaster here

explanation.surface: A bank's promise of money gets broken, as reported by a TV channel, and someone insists it's true.
explanation.definitionFit: I tell you is an emphatic interjection asserting certainty, just like that's for sure.

clue.text: Dogs spoilt garden seat

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Pet dogs have chewed and ruined the garden bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Danes are a very large breed of domestic dog.

clue.text: Could girl be put out?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint: a daughter is an example of offspring
definitions.meaning: first meaning: offspring, children, of which a girl could be one
second meaning: to release or publish

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a girl might be upset or annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'annoyed', but it means to release, as a magazine issues an edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in law means a person's children, and as a verb it means to send out or publish.

clue.text: Send back list including a bit of fish — large snapper?

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the whole string is read right to left
including here simply means together with, so the pieces are set side by side

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
the gill is the breathing organ of a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner returns an order because the list included a portion of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers the whole string; the 'a' sits after the fish part before it is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a big reptile with jaws that snap shut, hence a jocular large snapper.

clue.text: Mark good enough, if up to this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thin score or graze on a surface

definitions.text: good enough, if up to this?
definitions.note: a cryptic hint built on the idiom 'up to scratch'
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the standard in the idiom 'up to ...'

explanation.surface: A teacher's mark counts as good enough if it reaches this level.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a small surface mark, and being up to scratch means meeting the required standard.

clue.text: Some returned mail, a German sovereign's collection

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the run is read right to left
some means only a portion, so the letters are a run inside the clue words

parts.note: the run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: Part of the mail sent back by a German monarch's household.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the crown jewels and emblems of royalty, a monarch's collection of symbols.

clue.text: Surrey town remote, map leads to farm, all concluding

indicators.note: concluding means at the end, and all applies it to every word in the list, so each yields its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A remote Surrey town, where a map points the way to a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London; Epsom there is famous for its racecourse and the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a market town in Surrey, home of the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Show what one used to do for work?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large public exhibition

definitions.text: what one used to do for work?
definitions.note: a cryptic hint read as ex-position, a former job
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split as ex plus position, one's former post

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to demonstrate what their old job involved.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a public exhibition or display, and split it reads as a former job.

clue.text: Indian's centre spread shown

indicators.note: the centre of a word means its middle letters only

parts.note: the two middle letters of Indian
splayed means spread out wide

explanation.surface: An Indian newspaper's centre-page spread is on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Displayed means put on view or exhibited, so it is a synonym of shown.

clue.text: Rank place, occupant below

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means coming lower, so the occupant piece follows the place piece

parts.note: lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
a tenant occupies a property

explanation.surface: A list ranking a place, with its resident given underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a military rank, a junior commissioned officer.

clue.text: Pivotal moment, ace in tennis?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the stage beyond which you cannot turn back

definitions.note: a cryptic example rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read literally, a rally won because the serve came back unreturned

explanation.surface: A crucial turning point in a match, like serving an ace at tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a decisive stage after which retreat is impossible; an ace is a served winner the opponent never hits back.

clue.text: Fabulous gem India sent abroad

indicators.note: something sent abroad is scattered far and wide, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A wonderful jewel from India is exported overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like praise for the gem, but it means belonging to fable, not real.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its older sense means legendary or fictitious, like something merely dreamed up.

clue.text: Turner placing wife between insect and rat

indicators.note: placing something between two others puts it in the middle of a sequence of three

parts.note: a fly is an insect
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a heel and a rat are both contemptible people

explanation.surface: The painter Turner arranges his wife between an insect and a rat in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J.M.W. Turner, but it just means a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A flywheel is a heavy rotating wheel in a machine that stores momentum, so it is something that turns.

clue.text: Awful weight to bear, don't attack Lebanese port!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a roll of fat around the waist

definitions.note: a cryptic instruction read as spare Tyre
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a plea to ..., the city on the Lebanese coast

explanation.surface: A plea to an army carrying a terrible burden not to assault a Lebanese harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is informal for excess belly fat; read as two words it begs mercy for Tyre in Lebanon.

clue.text: Everything one owns ending in garbage, say

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of garbage
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that all their possessions end up as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is the whole of their property and possessions, especially at death.

clue.text: Spanish food: odd bits of that with juice on the counter

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first, third and so on, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of that

indicators.note: counter means going against, the opposite way, so the juice word is read backwards

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant

explanation.surface: Spanish snacks laid out on a bar counter, with fruit juice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small savoury dishes served in Spanish bars.

clue.text: Fairly fair

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like the same idea twice, but one is an adverb of degree and the other an adjective for beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty can be an adverb meaning moderately and an adjective meaning attractive, matching both senses.

clue.text: Securing runs, I thump ground in victory

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one letter goes into the other letters
something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman hits runs and pounds the turf in celebration of a win.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or success.

clue.text: Coaster circling south pole

indicators.note: circling something means going all the way round it, enclosing it

parts.note: a coaster is a small mat for a drink
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A coastal ship sails round the South Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaster' suggests a ship and 'south pole' the Antarctic, but the definition is just 'pole'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast is a tall upright pole, such as one carrying a ship's sails.

clue.text: Touching line from man with whip

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so the two pieces are simply put side by side

parts.note: to tan is to beat or thrash, as in 'tan his hide'
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A moving line spoken by a man holding a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line that touches a curve at one point.

clue.text: Still not accomplished? Bother!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as '...', still remaining on the list
second meaning: a fuss or commotion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bother!' looks like an exclamation of annoyance, but it is a noun for a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks still to do are unaccomplished, and a to-do is a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Rose late, lover set about throttling paramour for a start!

indicators.note: throttling grips something tight around its neck, so the letters wrap around it
about can mean turned around or in a different arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of paramour

explanation.surface: A jealous lover strangles a rival paramour, then wakes up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Overslept means slept past the intended time, so the sleeper got up late.

clue.text: Famous — as are Mozart's works?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint: music is written down in notes
definitions.meaning: second meaning: written in musical notes

explanation.surface: Something celebrated, like the compositions of Mozart.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means renowned, and a composer's music is literally set down in notes.
